A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IGG research despite the changed title and formatting. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation evaluations, guidance analyses, ablations, and an appendix experiment applying mixed CFG–IGG guidance to EDM2.

after.justification: v3 retains original image-generation evaluations and ablations, and additionally reports GenEval category scores and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The specified sampling rule changes locally. In v1, the guidance vector includes gamma_k before entering attention; v3 defines an unscaled vector and places gamma_k outside the softmax in Equation 6. These formulations are not algebraically equivalent because attention is nonlinear. The core attention-based procedure remains; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet class-conditioned generation and MJHQ, COCO, and GenEval text-to-image generation. The new GenEval breakdown disaggregates existing coverage. Removing the EDM2 application changes the evaluated backbone setting without removing a separately identified dataset or task.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in retained Tables 1–3 are unchanged. However, the CFG controls against mixed CFG–IGG on EDM2-S and EDM2-XXL disappear with v1 Appendix A.5 and Table 5. This is a limited removal of comparisons, although CFG and EDM2 remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: v3 introduces per-image inference-time and GFLOP evaluation and removes the fixed-schedule EDM2 mixed-guidance experiment. Retained benchmark resolutions, guidance settings, and sampling budgets remain unchanged, including 50,000 ImageNet images and one/four images per prompt for the respective text benchmarks.

E4.justification: v3 adds a six-category GenEval breakdown and computational-overhead analysis, while removing the diffusion-transfer investigation in v1 Appendix A.5. The mixed-guidance, fixed-schedule, and sliding-window ablations, metric sweeps, and retained qualitative case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for these comparisons. The added tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark tables, ablation values, and metric curves are unchanged apart from equivalent formatting. v3 adds category scores, including VAR-CLIP counting scores of 0.113 for CFG and 0.094 for IGG, plus timing/GFLOP results. It removes the EDM2 CFG/mixed-guidance FID pairs 2.29/2.20 and 1.84/1.82 from v1 Table 5.

T1.justification: Equations 2 and 6 revise the guidance-vector definition and placement of its scale. v3 also replaces v1's gamma_k := 1 + lambda_k relation with the inconsistent gamma_k := 1 + gamma_k. The explicit diffusion-mixture Equation 7 is removed. The divergence algorithm is retained, and neither version supplies formal proofs.

C1.justification: v3 narrows v1's claims of setting a new benchmark and surpassing state-of-the-art performance to improvements over baselines and the reported VAR comparisons. The three central contributions—guidance analysis, attention-based IGG, and class-conditioned/text-to-image evaluation—remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of category-specific prompt improvements and negligible computational overhead. It removes v1's speculative explanation for beneficial negative IGG weights in diffusion and the anticipated high-resolution efficiency benefit of sliding-window guidance. The central semantic-misalignment explanation remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link in the abstract. It removes v1's explanation that guidance operates on raw logits with overloaded probability notation, and loses the EDM2 adaptation details with Appendix A.5. The new timing table provides no hardware or timing-unit specification.

R1.justification: References to Endres and Schindelin's distance metric, Ho et al.'s DDPM, and Song et al.'s DDIM are removed. Most other bibliography changes update publication metadata for the same works. The related-work organization and claim of SwAR-specific guidance novelty remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, divergence explanation, and conclusion are revised, while most prose and the main section sequence remain. v3 adds a computational-cost subsection and generic impact statement, reformats the contributions, and relabels retained appendix subsections as Appendices A–D.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference-style document, substantially resizing and relocating displays. The first two figures exchange numbering and placement; retained graphics are largely unchanged. v3 adds GenEval and computational-cost tables, removes the diffusion-results table, and compresses several existing tables.

improvement.justification: Narrower claims, category-level diagnostics, and a code link improve transparency, but diffusion-transfer evidence is removed and the revised guidance formulation is not reconciled with the retained results or metric-scaling discussion. v3 introduces an inconsistent scale definition, and Table 5 reports +0.0004 where 0.7103 minus 0.7009 equals 0.0094. Whether the revised method specification corrects the earlier account remains unresolved, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
